paragraphs.en: Every Sunday morning, I go to the park near my house. The air is fresh, and the birds sing in the trees. Many people are already there when I arrive.
paragraphs.zh: 每個星期天早上，我都會去家附近的公園。空氣很清新，鳥兒在樹上唱歌。當我到達時，已經有許多人在那裡了。

paragraphs.en: Some old people do exercise together under a big tree. Children run and laugh on the grass. A young man plays the guitar and sings songs.
paragraphs.zh: 一些老人家在大樹下一起做運動。孩子們在草地上奔跑歡笑。一位年輕人彈著吉他唱歌。

paragraphs.en: I like to sit on a bench and read a book. Sometimes I just watch the people and smile. A simple morning in the park always makes me happy.
paragraphs.zh: 我喜歡坐在長椅上看書。有時候我只是看著人們，微笑著。公園裡簡單的早晨總是讓我很快樂。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I took my first cooking class. Our teacher was a friendly woman with twenty years of experience. She taught us how to make a simple pasta dish.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我上了第一堂烹飪課。我們的老師是一位友善的女士，有二十年的經驗。她教我們做一道簡單的義大利麵。

paragraphs.en: At first, I was nervous. I cut the vegetables too big, and I put too much salt in the sauce. The teacher smiled and said, "Don't worry. Everyone makes mistakes at the beginning."
paragraphs.zh: 起初我很緊張。我把蔬菜切得太大塊，醬汁裡放了太多鹽。老師微笑著說：「別擔心，每個人剛開始都會犯錯。」

paragraphs.en: After two hours, my pasta was ready. It was not perfect, but it tasted good. Now I cook dinner for my family every weekend. Cooking is my new hobby.
paragraphs.zh: 兩個小時後，我的義大利麵完成了。雖然不完美，但味道很好。現在我每個週末都為家人做晚餐。烹飪成了我的新嗜好。

paragraphs.en: One rainy evening, I found a small cat outside my door. It was wet and cold, and it looked very hungry. I gave it some food and a warm towel.
paragraphs.zh: 一個下雨的傍晚，我在門外發現一隻小貓。牠又濕又冷，看起來非常餓。我給了牠一些食物和一條溫暖的毛巾。

paragraphs.en: The next day, I made posters with the cat's picture. I put them around my neighborhood. Three days later, a little girl called me. She was crying with joy.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天，我做了印有貓咪照片的海報，貼在住家附近。三天後，一個小女孩打電話給我。她高興得哭了。

paragraphs.en: The cat's name was Coco, and it was her best friend. When they met again, Coco jumped into her arms. Helping them find each other was a wonderful feeling.
paragraphs.zh: 那隻貓的名字叫可可，是她最好的朋友。當他們再次見面時，可可跳進了她的懷裡。幫助他們重逢的感覺真美好。

title: A Trip to the Night Market

paragraphs.en: Taiwan is famous for its night markets. Last Friday, my foreign friend David visited me, and I took him to the biggest night market in the city.
paragraphs.zh: 台灣以夜市聞名。上週五，我的外國朋友大衛來找我，我帶他去市區最大的夜市。

paragraphs.en: David tried many kinds of food. He loved the fried chicken and the bubble tea. He was afraid of the stinky tofu at first, but after one bite, he asked for more!
paragraphs.zh: 大衛嘗試了很多種食物。他很喜歡炸雞和珍珠奶茶。他一開始不敢吃臭豆腐，但咬了一口之後，竟然還想再吃！

paragraphs.en: We also played games and won a small toy. David said it was the best night of his trip. Food, games, and friends - a night market has everything.
paragraphs.zh: 我們還玩了遊戲，贏得一個小玩具。大衛說這是他旅程中最棒的一晚。美食、遊戲和朋友——夜市什麼都有。

paragraphs.en: My daughter is six years old. Last week, she asked me to teach her how to ride a bicycle. We went to the school playground on Saturday morning.
paragraphs.zh: 我的女兒六歲了。上週，她請我教她騎腳踏車。星期六早上，我們去了學校的操場。

paragraphs.en: She fell down many times, but she did not cry. She stood up, smiled, and tried again. After two hours, she could ride slowly without my help.
paragraphs.zh: 她跌倒了很多次，但沒有哭。她站起來，微笑著再試一次。兩個小時後，她已經可以不用我扶，慢慢地騎了。

paragraphs.en: When she rode across the playground alone, she shouted, "Daddy, look at me!" I felt so proud. Children teach us that we should never give up.
paragraphs.zh: 當她獨自騎過操場時，她大喊：「爸爸，你看我！」我感到非常驕傲。孩子們教會我們永遠不要放棄。

paragraphs.en: Each season has its own beauty. In spring, flowers open and the world turns green. The weather is warm, and people like to walk outside.
paragraphs.zh: 每個季節都有自己的美。春天，花朵綻放，世界變成一片綠意。天氣溫暖，人們喜歡外出散步。

paragraphs.en: Summer brings hot days and bright sunshine. Families go to the beach and children swim in the sea. In autumn, the leaves turn red and yellow, and the air becomes cool.
paragraphs.zh: 夏天帶來炎熱的日子和明亮的陽光。全家人去海邊，孩子們在海裡游泳。秋天，樹葉轉紅變黃，空氣變得涼爽。

paragraphs.en: Winter is quiet and cold. In some places, snow covers the ground like a white blanket. People drink hot tea and stay warm at home. Which season do you like best?
paragraphs.zh: 冬天安靜而寒冷。在某些地方，白雪像一條白毯子覆蓋大地。人們喝著熱茶，待在溫暖的家裡。你最喜歡哪個季節呢？

title: A Letter to My Future Self

paragraphs.en: Dear future me, how are you? Today I am fifteen years old, and I am writing this letter in my English class. I want to ask you some questions.
paragraphs.zh: 親愛的未來的我，你好嗎？今天我十五歲，正在英文課上寫這封信。我想問你幾個問題。

paragraphs.en: Did you become a doctor like you dreamed? Do you still play basketball with your old friends? I hope you take care of Mom and Dad, and I hope you are happy.
paragraphs.zh: 你有沒有像夢想的那樣成為醫生？你還和老朋友們打籃球嗎？我希望你好好照顧爸爸媽媽，也希望你過得快樂。

paragraphs.en: Right now, I study hard every day. Sometimes it is difficult, but I will not stop. Future me, please remember: you were a brave kid with a big dream.
paragraphs.zh: 現在，我每天都努力讀書。有時候很辛苦，但我不會停下來。未來的我，請記住：你曾是一個懷抱大夢想的勇敢孩子。

paragraphs.en: Many people believe that sleeping less means achieving more. However, science tells a different story. Sleep is not wasted time; it is when our body repairs itself and our brain organizes memories.
paragraphs.zh: 許多人認為睡得少代表能完成更多事。然而，科學告訴我們並非如此。睡眠不是浪費時間；那是身體自我修復、大腦整理記憶的時刻。

paragraphs.en: Research shows that adults need seven to nine hours of sleep each night. People who sleep less than six hours have a higher risk of heart disease, weight gain, and depression. Lack of sleep also weakens our ability to focus and make decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 研究顯示，成年人每晚需要七到九小時的睡眠。睡不到六小時的人，罹患心臟病、體重增加和憂鬱症的風險較高。睡眠不足也會削弱我們專注和做決定的能力。

paragraphs.en: To sleep better, experts suggest keeping a regular schedule, avoiding screens before bedtime, and keeping the bedroom dark and quiet. Good sleep is not a luxury - it is a necessary part of a healthy life.
paragraphs.zh: 想要睡得更好，專家建議維持規律的作息、睡前避免使用螢幕，並保持臥室黑暗安靜。良好的睡眠不是奢侈品——而是健康生活不可或缺的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Most people fail to change their lives because they aim too high too quickly. They promise to exercise for an hour every day or to read fifty books a year. After two weeks, they give up and feel disappointed.
paragraphs.zh: 大多數人無法改變生活，是因為一開始就把目標訂得太高。他們承諾每天運動一小時，或一年讀五十本書。兩週之後就放棄了，並感到失望。

paragraphs.en: A better approach is to start with tiny habits. Instead of an hour of exercise, do five minutes. Instead of a whole book, read one page before bed. Small actions are easy to repeat, and repetition is what creates real change.
paragraphs.zh: 更好的方法是從微小的習慣開始。與其運動一小時，不如先做五分鐘。與其讀完一整本書，不如睡前讀一頁。小行動容易重複，而重複正是創造真正改變的關鍵。

paragraphs.en: Over time, these small habits grow naturally. Five minutes becomes twenty, and one page becomes one chapter. As the writer James Clear says, you do not rise to the level of your goals; you fall to the level of your systems.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著時間過去，這些小習慣會自然成長。五分鐘變成二十分鐘，一頁變成一章。正如作家詹姆斯・克利爾所說：你不會達到目標的高度，而是會落到系統的水準。

paragraphs.en: Coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world, but people enjoy it in very different ways. In Italy, people stand at a bar and finish a small espresso in two minutes. Ordering a large milky coffee after lunch is considered strange.
paragraphs.zh: 咖啡是世界上最受歡迎的飲品之一，但各地的人享用方式大不相同。在義大利，人們站在吧台前，兩分鐘內喝完一小杯濃縮咖啡。午餐後點一大杯加奶咖啡會被認為很奇怪。

paragraphs.en: In Turkey, coffee is cooked slowly in a small pot and served with sweets. It is so important to the culture that UNESCO added Turkish coffee to its cultural heritage list. In Sweden, people enjoy 'fika' - a daily coffee break with friends that is almost a national tradition.
paragraphs.zh: 在土耳其，咖啡用小壺慢慢煮，並搭配甜點享用。它對文化如此重要，聯合國教科文組織甚至將土耳其咖啡列入文化遺產名錄。在瑞典，人們享受「fika」——每天與朋友的咖啡時光，幾乎是一種全民傳統。

paragraphs.en: Whether it is a quick shot in Rome or a slow afternoon in Stockholm, coffee does the same job everywhere: it brings people together. The next time you travel, try drinking coffee the local way.
paragraphs.zh: 無論是在羅馬快速喝一杯，還是在斯德哥爾摩度過緩慢的午後，咖啡在世界各地的作用都一樣：把人們聚在一起。下次旅行時，不妨試著用當地的方式喝咖啡。

title: Should Students Use AI for Homework?
title_zh: 學生應該用 AI 寫作業嗎？

paragraphs.en: Artificial intelligence tools can now write essays, solve math problems, and answer almost any question. This creates a difficult question for schools: should students be allowed to use AI for their homework?
paragraphs.zh: 人工智慧工具現在可以寫文章、解數學題，回答幾乎任何問題。這為學校帶來一個難題：應該允許學生用 AI 寫作業嗎？

paragraphs.en: Some teachers worry that students will stop thinking for themselves. If AI writes your essay, you learn nothing about writing. Others argue that AI is like a calculator - a tool that everyone will use at work, so students should learn to use it well.
paragraphs.zh: 有些老師擔心學生會停止自己思考。如果 AI 幫你寫文章，你就學不到任何寫作能力。另一些人則認為 AI 就像計算機——是每個人工作時都會用到的工具，所以學生應該學會善用它。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the answer lies in the middle. Students can use AI to check grammar, get ideas, or understand difficult concepts, but the final thinking should be their own. The goal of education is not to produce perfect homework - it is to produce thinking people.
paragraphs.zh: 也許答案就在中間。學生可以用 AI 檢查文法、獲得靈感或理解困難的概念，但最終的思考應該是自己的。教育的目的不是產出完美的作業——而是培養會思考的人。

paragraphs.en: A honeybee colony is one of nature's most amazing societies. Up to 60,000 bees live together in a single hive, and each bee has a clear job. Workers collect food, guards protect the entrance, and the queen lays all the eggs.
paragraphs.zh: 蜂群是大自然最令人驚嘆的社會之一。多達六萬隻蜜蜂共同生活在一個蜂巢裡，每隻蜜蜂都有明確的工作。工蜂採集食物，守衛蜂保護入口，蜂后則負責產下所有的卵。

paragraphs.en: Bees even have their own language. When a worker finds flowers full of nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a special dance. The direction and speed of her dance tell other bees exactly where to find the food.
paragraphs.zh: 蜜蜂甚至有自己的語言。當工蜂發現滿是花蜜的花朵時，她會回到蜂巢跳一種特別的舞。舞蹈的方向和速度能準確告訴其他蜜蜂食物的位置。

paragraphs.en: Bees matter far beyond honey. About one third of the food we eat depends on their pollination. Protecting bees means protecting our own dinner table - a fact worth remembering the next time one buzzes past you.
paragraphs.zh: 蜜蜂的重要性遠不止於蜂蜜。我們吃的食物約有三分之一仰賴牠們授粉。保護蜜蜂就是保護我們自己的餐桌——下次有蜜蜂從你身邊嗡嗡飛過時，值得記住這一點。

paragraphs.en: Last month, I tried an experiment: I turned off my phone for an entire weekend. The first few hours were uncomfortable. My hand kept reaching for my pocket, and I felt strangely anxious, as if I were missing something important.
paragraphs.zh: 上個月，我做了一個實驗：整個週末關掉手機。最初幾個小時很不自在。我的手不斷伸向口袋，我感到莫名的焦慮，彷彿錯過了什麼重要的事。

paragraphs.en: By Saturday afternoon, something changed. I finished a novel I had started months ago. I cooked a proper meal instead of ordering delivery. In the evening, I had a three-hour conversation with my parents - without checking notifications once.
paragraphs.zh: 到了星期六下午，情況開始改變。我讀完了幾個月前開始看的小說。我好好煮了一頓飯，而不是叫外送。晚上，我和父母聊了三個小時——一次都沒有查看通知。

paragraphs.en: On Monday, I turned my phone back on. I had 47 messages, but honestly, none of them were urgent. The world had continued perfectly well without my attention. Now I take a phone-free evening every week, and I protect it like an important meeting.
paragraphs.zh: 星期一，我重新開機。有四十七則訊息，但說實話，沒有一則是緊急的。沒有我的關注，世界依然運轉得很好。現在我每週都安排一個不用手機的晚上，並像重要會議一樣守護這段時間。

title: How the Bullet Train Got Its Nose

paragraphs.en: Japan's bullet trains are famous for their speed, but early models had a serious problem. Every time a train exited a tunnel at high speed, it produced a loud boom that disturbed residents living nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 日本的子彈列車以速度聞名，但早期的車型有個嚴重的問題。每當列車高速駛出隧道時，都會產生巨大的聲響，干擾附近的居民。

paragraphs.en: An engineer named Eiji Nakatsu found the answer in nature. He was a birdwatcher, and he noticed that the kingfisher dives into water at high speed with almost no splash. Its long, narrow beak cuts smoothly through the change between air and water.
paragraphs.zh: 一位名叫中津英治的工程師在大自然中找到了答案。他是一位賞鳥愛好者，注意到翠鳥高速衝入水中時幾乎不會濺起水花。牠細長的鳥喙能順暢地穿過空氣與水之間的交界。

paragraphs.en: The team redesigned the train's front to copy the kingfisher's beak. The new train was not only quieter - it also used 15 percent less electricity and ran 10 percent faster. Nature had already solved the problem millions of years ago; engineers just needed to look.
paragraphs.zh: 團隊模仿翠鳥的喙重新設計了車頭。新列車不僅更安靜，還省了百分之十五的電力，速度快了百分之十。大自然早在數百萬年前就解決了這個問題；工程師只需要用心觀察。

paragraphs.en: Streaming has fundamentally transformed the music industry. Two decades ago, artists earned revenue primarily through album sales; today, the vast majority of listening happens on platforms that pay fractions of a cent per stream.
paragraphs.zh: 串流媒體徹底改變了音樂產業。二十年前，歌手主要靠專輯銷售賺取收入；如今，絕大多數的聆聽都發生在每次播放僅支付不到一美分的平台上。

paragraphs.en: This shift has produced winners and losers. Global superstars with billions of streams accumulate substantial income, while independent musicians often receive monthly payments that barely cover a meal. Consequently, many artists now rely on touring, merchandise, and brand partnerships as their primary sources of revenue.
paragraphs.zh: 這種轉變造就了贏家與輸家。擁有數十億次播放量的全球巨星累積了可觀的收入，而獨立音樂人每月拿到的錢往往連一頓飯都不夠。因此，許多歌手現在把巡演、周邊商品和品牌合作當作主要收入來源。

paragraphs.en: Critics argue the system is unsustainable, yet streaming has also democratized access: any musician can now reach a global audience without a record label. The question facing the industry is not whether streaming will survive, but whether a fairer distribution model can emerge from it.
paragraphs.zh: 批評者認為這種制度難以持續，但串流也讓機會變得更平等：任何音樂人現在都能不靠唱片公司接觸全球聽眾。產業面臨的問題不是串流能否存活，而是能否從中發展出更公平的分配模式。

paragraphs.en: Cities are consistently warmer than the countryside around them, a phenomenon scientists call the urban heat island effect. Concrete and asphalt absorb solar radiation during the day and release it slowly at night, keeping temperatures elevated around the clock.
paragraphs.zh: 城市總是比周圍的鄉村更溫暖，科學家稱這種現象為都市熱島效應。混凝土和柏油在白天吸收太陽輻射，夜間再緩慢釋放，使氣溫全天維持在較高的水準。

paragraphs.en: The consequences extend beyond discomfort. Higher temperatures increase electricity demand for air conditioning, worsen air pollution, and pose genuine health risks to elderly residents. During heat waves, urban neighborhoods with few trees record significantly more hospital admissions than greener districts.
paragraphs.zh: 其後果不僅止於不舒適。更高的氣溫增加了空調用電需求、惡化空氣污染，並對年長居民構成實際的健康風險。熱浪期間，樹木稀少的市區社區就醫人數明顯高於綠化較多的地區。

paragraphs.en: Fortunately, solutions exist and are relatively affordable. Planting street trees, painting rooftops white, and preserving urban parks can lower local temperatures by several degrees. The challenge is not technical but political: cities must prioritize long-term livability over short-term development profits.
paragraphs.zh: 幸運的是，解決方案是存在的，而且成本相對低廉。種植行道樹、將屋頂漆成白色、保留城市公園，都能讓局部氣溫降低好幾度。挑戰不在技術，而在政治：城市必須把長期宜居性置於短期開發利益之上。

paragraphs.en: Procrastination is commonly misunderstood as laziness or poor time management. Psychological research suggests otherwise: procrastination is primarily an emotional regulation problem. We delay tasks not because we cannot schedule them, but because they trigger negative feelings - boredom, anxiety, or self-doubt.
paragraphs.zh: 拖延常被誤解為懶惰或不會管理時間。心理學研究卻指出並非如此：拖延主要是情緒調節的問題。我們延遲任務，不是因為排不出時間，而是因為這些任務引發了負面情緒——無聊、焦慮或自我懷疑。

paragraphs.en: When we avoid a difficult task, we feel immediate relief, and the brain registers this relief as a reward. This creates a vicious cycle: each avoidance strengthens the habit, while the postponed task grows more intimidating. Paradoxically, people often procrastinate most on the goals they care about most deeply.
paragraphs.zh: 當我們逃避困難的任務時，會立刻感到輕鬆，而大腦會把這種輕鬆記錄為一種獎勵。這形成了惡性循環：每一次逃避都強化了這個習慣，而被延後的任務則變得越來越可怕。矛盾的是，人們最常拖延的，往往是自己最在乎的目標。

paragraphs.en: Effective remedies therefore target emotions rather than calendars. Breaking work into trivially small steps reduces the fear of starting; practicing self-compassion after setbacks prevents the shame spiral that fuels further delay. The counterintuitive lesson is that forgiving yourself for procrastinating is one of the most effective ways to stop doing it.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，有效的解方針對的是情緒，而不是行事曆。把工作拆成極小的步驟能降低開始的恐懼；在挫折後練習自我疼惜，能避免助長進一步拖延的羞愧漩渦。反直覺的啟示是：原諒自己的拖延，正是停止拖延最有效的方法之一。

title: What Octopuses Teach Us About Intelligence

paragraphs.en: The octopus presents a fascinating puzzle for scientists studying intelligence. Its last common ancestor with humans was a simple worm that lived 600 million years ago, yet octopuses solve mazes, open jars, use tools, and appear to play - abilities we normally associate with mammals and birds.
paragraphs.zh: 對研究智慧的科學家而言，章魚是個迷人的謎題。牠與人類最近的共同祖先是六億年前的一種簡單蠕蟲，然而章魚會走迷宮、開罐子、使用工具，甚至似乎會玩耍——這些能力我們通常只與哺乳類和鳥類聯想在一起。

paragraphs.en: Their intelligence is organized in a radically different way. Two thirds of an octopus's neurons reside not in its brain but in its arms, which can taste, touch, and make decisions semi-independently. In a sense, each arm has a mind of its own, and the central brain acts more like a coordinator than a commander.
paragraphs.zh: 牠們的智慧以截然不同的方式組織。章魚三分之二的神經元不在大腦，而在牠的腕足裡；這些腕足能嚐味道、有觸覺，並且能半獨立地做決定。某種意義上，每條腕足都有自己的心智，而中央大腦更像協調者，而非指揮官。

paragraphs.en: This matters because octopuses demonstrate that intelligence is not a single ladder with humans at the top, but a landscape with multiple peaks. Evolution invented minds at least twice, through entirely different architectures. If we ever encounter intelligence beyond Earth, the octopus reminds us it may look nothing like our own.
paragraphs.zh: 這件事之所以重要，是因為章魚證明了智慧不是一座以人類為頂端的階梯，而是一片擁有多座山峰的地景。演化至少用完全不同的架構「發明」了兩次心智。如果有一天我們遇到地球以外的智慧，章魚提醒我們：它可能與我們的智慧毫無相似之處。

title: The Hidden Cost of Fast Fashion

paragraphs.en: Fast fashion has made clothing astonishingly cheap and abundant. A t-shirt costs less than a sandwich, and new styles arrive in stores every week. Yet this convenience conceals substantial costs that never appear on the price tag.
paragraphs.zh: 快時尚讓衣服變得驚人地便宜且大量。一件 T 恤比一份三明治還便宜，而且新款式每週都會上架。然而，這種便利掩蓋了從未出現在價格標籤上的龐大代價。

paragraphs.en: The environmental burden is severe: the fashion industry consumes enormous quantities of water, and produces roughly ten percent of global carbon emissions - more than international flights and shipping combined. Meanwhile, the majority of discarded clothing ends up in landfills, often in developing countries that never asked to receive it.
paragraphs.zh: 環境負擔十分沉重：時尚產業消耗大量的水，並產生全球約百分之十的碳排放——比國際航空和海運加起來還多。同時，大多數被丟棄的衣物最終進了垃圾掩埋場，而且往往落在從未要求接收它們的開發中國家。

paragraphs.en: Consumers are not powerless, however. Buying fewer, higher-quality garments, choosing second-hand clothing, and simply wearing clothes longer can significantly reduce this impact. Research suggests that extending a garment's life by just nine months reduces its environmental footprint by twenty to thirty percent. The most sustainable shirt, it turns out, is the one already in your closet.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，消費者並非無能為力。少買一些、選擇品質更好的衣物、購買二手衣，或單純把衣服穿久一點，都能顯著減少這種影響。研究指出，只要將一件衣服的壽命延長九個月，就能減少百分之二十到三十的環境足跡。事實證明，最環保的襯衫，就是你衣櫃裡已經有的那一件。

title: Remote Work and the Future of Cities
title_zh: 遠距工作與城市的未來

paragraphs.en: The pandemic proved that millions of jobs can be performed from anywhere with a laptop and a stable connection. Years later, the consequences are still reshaping urban economies in ways few predicted.
paragraphs.zh: 疫情證明了數百萬份工作只要有筆電和穩定的網路，在任何地方都能完成。多年後，其後果仍在以少有人預料到的方式重塑城市經濟。

paragraphs.en: Downtown districts built around office workers have suffered the most. Coffee shops, dry cleaners, and lunch restaurants lost their weekday customers, and some office towers report vacancy rates above thirty percent. Meanwhile, smaller towns and suburbs have experienced an influx of remote professionals seeking space and affordability, driving up housing prices far from traditional job centers.
paragraphs.zh: 圍繞上班族打造的市中心區受創最深。咖啡店、乾洗店和午餐餐廳失去了平日的顧客，一些辦公大樓的空置率超過百分之三十。與此同時，較小的城鎮和郊區湧入了尋求空間與可負擔生活的遠距工作者，推高了遠離傳統就業中心地區的房價。

paragraphs.en: Cities now face a choice: adapt or decline. Some are converting empty offices into apartments; others are redesigning downtowns around culture and entertainment rather than commuting. The office is not dead, but its monopoly on work has ended - and the cities that thrive will be those that give people reasons beyond employment to gather.
paragraphs.zh: 城市現在面臨抉擇：轉型或衰退。有些城市正把空辦公室改建成住宅；有些則圍繞文化和娛樂而非通勤重新設計市中心。辦公室並未消亡，但它對工作的壟斷已經結束——能夠繁榮的城市，將是那些能給人們「就業以外」相聚理由的城市。
